checkpoints.name: Move runtime logs into the repository
checkpoints.scope: Change the default log location from the system temporary directory to a logs directory at the Git repository root, while preserving the explicit --log-dir override and treating generated logs as tracked audit artifacts that are included in checkpoint commits.
exit_criteria: The default log directory resolves to <git-repository-root>/logs regardless of the caller's current working directory
An explicit --log-dir value continues to take precedence over the repository-local default
The logs directory is created when needed and its generated audit logs are eligible for Git tracking and automated checkpoint commits
Tests cover repository-root resolution, directory creation, explicit overrides, and inclusion of generated logs in checkpoint staging
checkpoints.review_notes:
Phase 0 complete.

Files touched:
- src/agent_loop/safety.py: default_log_dir() resolves to git_ops.repo_root() / 'logs'.
- src/agent_loop/git_ops.py: commit_checkpoint_changes() includes log directory in staging (removed exclude pattern).
- tests/test_safety.py: Added unit tests for default log directory resolution from root/subdirectories, GitError when outside git, and directory creation on file open/tee.
- tests/test_git_ops.py: Added unit tests for repo root resolution, staging/committing generated logs in checkpoint commits, cwd invariance, and clean worktree no-op.
- tests/test_cli.py: Added tests for CLI --log-dir override and default log dir fallback.
- tests/test_orchestrator.py: Added tests verifying run_loop passes explicit log_dir or defaults to safety.default_log_dir().

Exit criteria met:
1. safety.default_log_dir() resolves to <git-repo-root>/logs from any working directory.
2. Explicit --log-dir overrides repository default in CLI and orchestrator.
3. safety.open_log_file() creates the directory, logs/ is not gitignored, and commit_checkpoint_changes() tracks and commits audit logs.
4. Comprehensive pytest suite tests repository resolution, directory creation, override precedence, and log commit staging.

checkpoints.name: Capture a complete agent-loop audit trail
checkpoints.scope: Extend each run's repository-local log so it records developer and reviewer agent traces plus structured lifecycle entries for checkpoint commits, requested review changes, and approvals. Ensure records are ordered, attributable to their role and checkpoint, and useful even when a run halts or a commit is unnecessary.
exit_criteria: Developer and reviewer traces from every initial, review, and revision invocation are written to the run log with role and checkpoint context
Every checkpoint commit attempt is logged with its requested commit statement and outcome, including the created commit identifier or an explicit no-change result
Reviewer change requests are logged as review comments and successful reviews are logged as approval comments without relying only on mutable plan state
Audit entries preserve chronological ordering, are flushed after completed events, and are committed so reviewers can inspect the durable run history after success, failure, or a halted run
The commit workflow records commit outcomes without losing them between checkpoint commits and leaves no completed audit entries uncommitted at the end of a successful run
Tests cover successful approval, requested revisions, no-op commits, and halted or failed execution without invoking real agent CLIs
checkpoints.review_notes:
Phase 1 complete.

Files touched:
- src/agent_loop/git_ops.py: Added CommitResult dataclass; enhanced commit_checkpoint_changes() to log commit attempt statements, outcomes with commit SHAs or explicit no-change results; updated require_clean_worktree(log_dir=None) to permit active log files.
- src/agent_loop/orchestrator.py: Enhanced run_loop() with structured lifecycle logging (role and checkpoint context for developer/reviewer initial, review, and revision invocations); logged reviewer change requests as review comments and approvals as approval comments; flushed events; added durable history commits on halt (f"{cid}: halted"), failure ("audit: run failed"), and completion ("audit: completed run").
- tests/test_git_ops.py: Added unit tests for commit attempt and commit ID outcome logging, explicit no-change logging, sequential commit outcome preservation, and real git repo end-to-end runs for approved and halted execution.
- tests/test_orchestrator.py: Updated lifecycle tests for audit completion commits; added unit tests for traces with role and checkpoint context, reviewer change requests, revision trails, halted execution, and failure states.

Exit criteria met:
1. Developer and reviewer traces from initial, review, and revision invocations are logged with role ([developer], [reviewer]) and checkpoint context ([{cid}]).
2. Every checkpoint commit attempt logs its requested commit statement and outcome (commit SHA or explicit no-change result) via CommitResult.
3. Reviewer change requests and approvals are logged as review comments and approval comments without relying only on mutable plan state.
4. Chronological ordering is preserved, events are flushed immediately, and durable run history is committed on success, halt, or failure.
5. Commit outcomes are preserved across sequential checkpoint commits and finalized at run end leaving no uncommitted audit entries.
6. Pytest suite tests approval, revisions, no-op commits, halted runs, and failure handling without invoking real agent CLIs.

checkpoints.name: Document and verify repository-local logging
checkpoints.scope: Document the default logs directory, override behavior, log contents, and Git hygiene, then run the complete automated test suite to verify the logging changes do not regress the checkpoint loop.
exit_criteria: README documentation identifies ./logs at the repository root as the default and explains --log-dir precedence
README documentation states that logs include agent traces, commit statements and outcomes, review comments, and approval comments
README documentation explains that runtime logs are committed by the loop as reviewable audit artifacts and may contain agent output
The full python3 -m pytest suite passes
checkpoints.review_notes:
